# Blackline 0.15.46

Four things that were visibly wrong, and short invites.

## Fixed

- **Channel rows stopped jumbling.** The row is a three-column grid and the settings cog added in
  0.15.42 was a fourth child, so it wrapped onto a second line. The lock, the voice cluster and the
  cog share one cell now, and another trailing thing later cannot break the row.
- **The search filter list lines up.** Each syntax hint was pushed right on its own row, so they
  started wherever that row's title happened to end and the longer ones were cut short. The rows
  share the popup's own columns now: every hint starts in the same place and none are truncated.
- **The profile card stopped jumping to the cursor.** It was made visible before it was positioned,
  so it painted one frame at wherever it was last opened and then moved. It is laid out and placed
  while still invisible.
- **Somebody online in a direct conversation is online in a space too.** A space member's presence
  came from the space view, which is only recomputed when a space record changes — so it went stale
  between records and the same person read online in one place and offline in the other. The roster
  asks the live link first now.

## Short invites

An invite to a space can be a username and a code:

    @derek/wdnHS8MhmArrW9eb3i1HTg

Thirty-five characters instead of eighteen hundred. The name is resolved through the same registry
lookup that adding a person by username already uses; the code is presented on the knock, and the
inviter's device recognises its own code and knows which space it was for. Nothing about the space
travels with the code — the joiner builds the space from the owner's own signed record when it
arrives, guarded three ways: only a `create` record, only when the owner it names is the key that
signed it, and only from somebody a code went to in the last two minutes.

**Both forms, one box.** The sheet shows the short one when this device holds a username and the
long one otherwise, with the other always one click away, and says what each costs: redeeming a
short invite tells the name log that somebody asked about that name — not which space, and not who
asked — while the long one asks nothing of anybody. Pasting either into **Add someone** works; the
app tells them apart.

Verified end to end on two real cores: a second device given nothing but the short code ends up in
the space with its real name and channels.

## Also

- **Claiming a username now catches itself up.** The claim was sent and never synced, so the device
  did not know it held its own name until the next automatic sync — and would not offer a short
  invite, which depends on knowing. A claim syncs a few times over the following half minute.
- Two ways to answer "what name do I hold" had grown; there is one again.
